traits.leaf_arrangement.note: APweb, Brassicales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): leaves spiral. Opposite in Salvadoraceae and Bataceae only.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): leaves spiral (Moringaceae, Limnanthaceae spiral too).

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): compound leaves only in Akaniaceae, Moringaceae, Cleomaceae, some Caricaceae and Tropaeolaceae; Brassicaceae (most species) simple, often lobed.

traits.division_pattern.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): Limnanthaceae pinnate or pinnately lobed, Moringaceae and Akania odd-pinnate; palmate in Tropaeolaceae, Caricaceae, Cleomaceae. Brassicaceae lobing mostly pinnatifid (weighting inferred).

traits.rosette.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): woody families and vines leafy-stemmed; basal rosettes only in many Brassicaceae and Resedaceae, which state their own.

traits.inflorescence.note: APweb, Brassicales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): inflorescence racemose. Single flowers in Tropaeolaceae and Limnanthaceae (state their own).

traits.flowering_position.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): racemes end the shoots in the bulk of the order; axillary flowers in Tropaeolaceae, Limnanthaceae, Caricaceae, Setchellanthaceae. Weighting inferred from Brassicaceae.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): monosymmetric in Tropaeolaceae, Moringaceae, weakly Bretschneidera; Brassicaceae regular.

traits.zygomorphy.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): zygomorphic flowers (Tropaeolum, Moringa, Cleome, Reseda) are spurred or oblique, not lipped or pea-type.

traits.flower_merosity.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16) gives 3-5-merous Limnanthaceae, 6-merous Setchellanthus; Brassicaceae (over 3/4 of species) 4-merous; Wikipedia, Caper (read 2026-10-16): 4 sepals, 4 petals. Typical 4 by species weight.

traits.corolla_shape.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): petals free, often clawed, spreading; Brassicaceae already state rotate.

traits.hypanthium.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): floral cups only in small families (Tropaeolaceae spur-bearing receptacle, Moringaceae, Limnanthaceae).

traits.ovary_position.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): ovaries superior throughout, often stalked.

traits.stamens.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): Tropaeolaceae 8, Moringaceae 5, Akania 10, Caricaceae 10, Limnanthaceae 2 x calyx; Brassicaceae 6 (four long, two short). Typical 6 by species weight.

traits.carpels.note: APweb, Brassicales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): carpels 3 at the base of the order, but Brassicaceae, Cleomaceae and Capparaceae (most species) have 2.

traits.sexual_system.note: APweb, Brassicales page (read 2026-10-16): Caricaceae always unisexual; Batis dioecious or monoecious (Wikipedia, Batis (read 2026-10-16)); the rest bisexual.
